Replay

Authenticated short-lived relay credentials

4 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
ProtocolCoturn and timeGodot integrationVerification and remaining limits

replay/relay issues Coturn-compatible, time-limited credentials to an enabled room member. The provider retains its signing secret; clients receive only TURN URLs, a temporary username/password and expiry. This is independent of gameplay authority, process registration, room admission and checkpoint storage.

Protocol#

The client authenticates with its already-provisioned member control key. A fresh client nonce and increasing request sequence identify each acquisition. First it requests a challenge; then it authenticates an Acquire containing the returned challenge. Challenges belong to the physical transport connection and expire after five seconds. An Acquire captured on another connection, after expiry, or before a provider restart cannot mint a new credential.

An exact Acquire retry on the original connection returns the same issued expiry within the challenge window. It does not extend the credential lifetime. Membership is checked again on every request. hub_authorize uses the room's current enabled member and private control key; poisoned/unknown rooms do not issue credentials. This authorizes relay use, not possession of an active gameplay lease. Actual game participation still passes current incarnation, rendezvous and authority checks.

Canonical request/reply envelopes use version 1 and kinds 0x5451/0x5452, with direction-separated HMAC-SHA256. Replies bind the exact request hash, nonce, sequence, room, content and member. Fixed message bounds are 2048 bytes, four TURN URLs, a 96-byte username and a 64-byte password field. The provider retains at most 128 connection challenges, with global and per-connection work budgets.

Transport must authenticate the provider and keep replies confidential. HMAC does not encrypt a credential. The room service uses verified WSS deployments or its explicit loopback-only test mode. No relay secret or temporary password belongs in a URL, invitation, gameplay checkpoint or public log.

Coturn and time#

Coturn's REST-style credential is a timestamp-prefixed username and a Base64 HMAC-SHA1 password. Only this compatibility calculation uses legacy SHA-1; Replay request/reply authentication uses HMAC-SHA256. Known short-key and long-key vectors are checked independently, and real Coturn accepts the issued credentials. Coturn configuration.

The provider's clock supplies Unix seconds for TURN expiry and monotonic milliseconds for request budgets/challenge deadlines. Backward wall/monotonic samples poison the provider. Issuer and TURN-server clocks must be synchronized; the protocol cannot prove the clock of a separately operated relay. TTL is configured from 5–3600 seconds (the example service defaults to 600). Existing issued credentials may remain usable at TURN until expiry even if membership is later disabled.

The client does not trust its own wall clock to determine expiry. It starts the usable lifetime at its local request time and subtracts a one-second safety margin, never adding response latency. The client refreshes halfway through that interval. An unexpired credential remains available during a temporary refresh failure; an expired one does not. A membership denial retires the client cache immediately. Old replies cannot satisfy a different acquisition.

Godot integration#

Relay_Connection owns a verified WebSocket and the client protocol. It reconnects with a new connection-bound challenge, refreshes credentials while pumped, and builds validated ICE JSON from a usable grant. Its relay_ice_source returns nothing after expiry. Rtc_Config.ice_source is consulted before each new peer connection; an unavailable source fails that connection instead of falling back to direct ICE. Existing peer connections are not renegotiated merely because a credential refreshes.

Party_Config.relay_credentials=true enables this flow after durable enrollment. Party waits for a usable initial credential, then continues pumping refresh while the game is running. Room carries the source callback through migration/reconnect. Party and its relay owner must outlive any Room using that callback. Static ice_json and the provider option are mutually exclusive. Games opt in with REPLAY_CAVE_ROOM_RELAY=1 / RSY_ROOM_RELAY=1 or browser room_relay=1.

The standalone room service accepts:

Setting Meaning
REPLAY_ROOM_TURN_SECRET_FILE Private file containing the same strong secret configured in Coturn
REPLAY_ROOM_TURN_URLS One to four comma-separated TURN URLs
REPLAY_ROOM_TURN_TTL Credential lifetime in seconds, default 600
REPLAY_ROOM_TURN_RELAY_ONLY=1 Require relay-only candidate selection in issued ICE settings

Configure Coturn with use-auth-secret and the matching server-only secret. The fixture does this inside a private temporary directory. The service must be pumped serially with its shared transport/room hub; credentials are not durable authority decisions and do not alter their record formats or epochs.

Verification and remaining limits#

Shell
nix develop --command bash tests/replay_relay/run.sh
TURNSERVER=/path/to/turnserver REPLAY_TURN_PROVIDER=1 \
nix develop --command bash tests/replay_turn/run.sh

The provider fixture uses a short TTL, waits beyond the credential used for the initial selected connection, then migrates/rejoins with later credentials. See recorded evidence.

This is not instant revocation of credentials already known to a client, encrypted credential storage, a public relay deployment, or per-account billing enforcement. Operator clock synchronization, provider/relay quotas, public WSS/TLS, long-duration and combined-outage coverage remain required deployment work. The optional source does not implement in-place ICE restart; it supplies current credentials when a new connection is created.
